Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:21: In the midrash (Devarim Rabbah 9:3), they explain the verse (Ecclesiastes 8:8) "no man has power over the spirit, to retain the spirit," concerning death - their words: Rabbi Yehudah said, a person has no power over the Angel of Death to be rid of him, and "spirit" refers only to an angel, as it is said (Psalms 104:4) "who makes His angels spirits." Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta said, a person cannot make a weapon and be saved from the Angel of Death, as it is said, "He made shields for the spirit"; "and there is no authority on the day of death" - a person has no authority to say, "wait for me until I settle my accounts and instruct my household, and then I will come" - therefore it is said, "and there is no authority on the day of death" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:22: Rabbi Abba himself explains (Zohar, Vayakhel 199a) further particulars concerning matters of death, giving the parable of the story of Jonah the prophet, who was in a ship and was cast into the sea - like the soul when it is in the body in this world, and after its departure the body is cast into the grave, and the grave is the fish that swallowed Jonah. He says, of blessed memory: Jonah, who descended into the ship, is the soul of a person who descends into this world to be in a person's body. Why is it called "Jonah" [dove/oppressed]? Because once it joins with the body, it is then "oppressed" [yonah] in this world, along the lines of what is said (Leviticus 25:17) "you shall not wrong [tonu] one another"; and then a person goes about in this world like a ship in a great sea, which is thought to be about to break, as it says (Jonah 1:4) "and the ship was thought to be broken."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:23: When a person is in this world and sins, and thinks he can flee from before his Master and pays no heed in this world, then the Holy One, blessed be He, casts a mighty storm wind - this is the sentence of judgment that always stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, and demands judgment against the person. This is what stirs the ship and recalls the person's sins to seize him; once the person is seized by that storm in his sickbed, what is written? (Jonah 1:5) "and Jonah went down into the innermost parts of the ship and lay down and fell into a deep sleep" - even though the person is in his sickbed, his soul is not aroused to return before his Master to atone for his sins. What is written? (ibid.) "and the captain approached him" - who is the captain? This is the good inclination, who directs everything - "and said to him, why are you sleeping? Arise, call upon your God," etc. - this is not a time to sleep, for they are bringing you up for judgment for everything you did in this world; repent of your sin, consider these words, and return to your Master. "What is your occupation" - which you were engaged in in this world - and confess it before your Master. "And whence do you come" - consider whence you came, from a putrid drop, and do not be proud before Him. "What is your country" - consider that you were created from the earth and to the earth you will return. "And of what people are you" - consider whether you have the merit of the forefathers to protect you.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:24: Once they bring him up for judgment above, that storm, which is the sentence of judgment stirring against the person, demands from the King to judge those held captive by the King, and they all come one by one before Him. At that hour they draw near to the court; some of them open in merit and some open in guilt, and the sentence of judgment demands judgment; and if that person is not meritorious, what is written? (ibid. 1:13) "and the men rowed hard to return to dry land, but they could not" - those who spoke of his merit strive to return him to this world, but they cannot. Why? "For the sea grew more and more stormy against them" - the sentence of judgment goes and rages in the person's sins and overpowers them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:25: Then three appointed messengers descend upon him: one who writes down all the merits and all the sins the person did in this world; one who reckons his days; and one who accompanied him when he was in his mother's womb. We have established that the sentence of judgment does not subside until that time of which it is written (ibid. 15) "and they took up Jonah" - "and they took him up" - when they take him from his house to the graveyard, then they proclaim concerning him: if he is meritorious, they proclaim concerning him and say, "give honor to the image of the King - peace shall come, they shall rest on their couches, he who walked uprightly" (Isaiah 57:2). From where do we derive this? As it is written (ibid. 58:8) "and your righteousness shall walk before you, the glory of the Lord shall gather you." And if he is wicked, they proclaim concerning him and say, "woe to so-and-so, it would have been better for him not to have been created." Then what is written? (Jonah 1:15) "and they cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its raging." When they bring him into the graveyard, which is a place of judgment, then the sentence of judgment that was raging subsides from its fury.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:26: And the fish that swallowed him - this is the grave. What is written? (ibid. 2:1) "and Jonah was in the belly of the fish" - the innards of the fish are the belly of Sheol; from where do we derive this? As it is written (ibid. 2:3) "out of the belly of Sheol I cried" - and he was in the belly of the fish and called it the belly of Sheol. "Three days and three nights" - these are the three days a person is in the grave and his innards burst; after three days, that filth turns over on his face and says to him, "take what you gave me - you ate and drank every day and did not give to the poor, and all your days were like festivals and holidays, while the poor were hungry and did not eat with you; take what you gave me" - this is [the meaning of] (Malachi 2:3) "and I will scatter dung upon your faces," etc., as we have established.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:27: After this, from the third day onward, the person is judged from his eyes, his hands, and his feet - and this has been established, up to thirty days. All those thirty days the soul and the body are judged together, and therefore the soul is found below in the earth, not ascending to its place, like a woman who sits outside for the days of her impurity. Afterward the soul ascends and the body decays in the earth, until the time the Holy One, blessed be He, is aroused for the dead, and a certain voice is prepared to be aroused in the graveyard, saying (Isaiah 26:19) "awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for your dew is the dew of lights, and the earth shall cast out the shades" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:28: In the Tikkunim (53b), the matter of Jonah in the ship is given a different parable, but nevertheless, on the verse "arise, call upon your God," it agrees with the words of the Zohar - his words: "'arise, call upon your God' - referring to the supernal Shechinah, who desires you, and repent to her, to your Master, who is the Holy One, blessed be He. Consider that an evil maidservant rules over you, which is a putrid drop, and of her it is said (Job 1:7) 'and the Lord said to Satan, whence do you come' - for all sins are from the limbs of the putrid drop, since it is said to the wicked, in this regard, know whence you came, from a putrid drop - 'and the men rowed hard to return to dry land' in repentance 'but they could not, for the sea,' which is the sentence of judgment, 'grew more and more stormy against them'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:29: Further, concerning matters of death and reckoning, I found, in the manuscript "Margenita of Rabbi Meir," peace be upon him, words speaking of this - his words: "the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, neither sufferings nor rebukes nor warnings nor promises nor being uprooted [into exile] nor length of days nor patience nor a messenger nor a command nor curses nor bans nor consolations nor shame nor fear nor the dread of the World to Come nor the dread of the reckoning nor the dread of the judgment of Gehinnom nor My Name being profaned among the nations through you will benefit you." And whoever has all these deeds against him loses his merit and is withheld from much good, his years are shortened, he acquires a bad name, and his deeds and sins and the sins of his ancestors are remembered against him, and his prayer is rejected in this world and the World to Come, and all his deeds are made public and he is judged and reckoned for them, and every joy he rejoiced in through his inclination becomes mourning for him, and these are demanded of him with strange judgments and much shame, and cruel angels in the eternal world; therefore it says (Isaiah 10:3) "and what will you do on the day of reckoning," etc., "and where will you leave your glory?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:30: Further, one who sins with his eyes - his eyes grow dim; one who sins with his ears - he hears his own disgrace; one who sins with his mouth - his words are not heeded; one who sins in counsel - his livelihood diminishes; one who sins in thought - the radiance of his face changes; one who sins with his tongue - sufferings come upon him; one who sins with his hand - he descends from his honor; one who sins with his heart - he dies of worry; one who sins with his feet - his years are shortened; one who sins with his inclination - his inclination accuses him; one who sins and causes others to sin - buries his wife and his children and the members of his household; one who sins with mockery - his sentence is sealed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:31: What benefit is there for a person, whose end is to depart from world to world, from life to death, from light to darkness, from sweet sleep to cramped and bitter sleep, from sweet light to worm and maggot, from sweet delicacies to the taste of dust, from a pleasant embrace to an embrace of dust? How many wealthy men left the world crestfallen; how many wise men had their wisdom become a stumbling block to them; how many mighty men had their might become a stumbling block to them; how many raisers of children did not rejoice in their children; how many beautiful ones had their beauty become a stumbling block to them; how many elders did not see honor; how many young men were cut down at their wedding canopy!
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:32: What benefit is there in eating food that brings a person to many judgments, in joy that brings a person to much worry, in clothing that causes many misfortunes, in imagination that causes much pain, in sweet sleep that causes a strange death, in sin that destroys much merit, in complaint that deprives much livelihood?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:33: Who is a person of the World to Come? One who distances himself from transgressions and from improper imagination and from mockery and from slander and from ugliness and the like, and who fulfills the commandments and has a mitzvah in his hand performed truthfully, and distances himself from sin and from empty prayer, and confesses his sins before the Holy One, blessed be He, and does repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:34: Whoever associates with a wicked person drives himself away from this world and the World to Come; whoever shows a cheerful face to a wicked person is among those who anger God; whoever deceives in his ways mourns in the end; whoever leads his fellow from a good way to a bad way dies in the midst of his days; whoever mocks the commandments receives no mercy from Heaven; whoever mocks the poverty of the poor - in the end, he toils and others eat his toil; and whoever habitually makes his fellow's face turn red [with shame], his ledger is opened that very day; and there is nothing worse than one who occupies himself with vain matters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:35: Woe to one whom the world deceives; woe to one for whom the moment plays a trick; woe to one whose defender becomes his accuser; woe to one whose inclination overcomes him; woe to one against whom the wheel of fortune turns; woe to one who loses his labor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:36: There is punishment that comes immediately, and punishment that comes after a time; there is one that comes after another, and there are all that come at once; some come upon a person while he is awake, and some while he is asleep; some are heavy and some are like a passing breeze; some come with his knowledge and some without his knowledge; some in his old age and some in his youth; some in secret and some in public; some at home and some while traveling. Every trouble, distress, envy, breach, and misfortune diminishes the sin [i.e., serves as atonement].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:37: There is one who serves the Omnipresent out of fear, so that his livelihood not be cut off; there is one out of love; there is one out of shame; there is one out of simplicity; there is one in order to be seen; there is one with joy that a mitzvah came about through him; and there is one out of sufferings, as it is said (Hosea 5:15) "in their affliction they will seek Me early"; and each one according to his deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:38: At the time a person departs, the angel appointed over judgment stands opposite him and says to him, "woe to this body that has left the world empty of merits and full of sins." He looks at his feet and says, "woe to the feet that did not walk uprightly"; "woe to the hands that occupied themselves with falsehood"; "woe to the innards that benefited from theft"; "woe to the eyes that did not walk in faithfulness"; "woe to the ears that did not accept rebuke"; "woe to the mouth that did not occupy itself with Torah"; "woe to the flesh that did not toil in fear"; "woe to the inclination that did not submit before its Creator"; "woe to the heart that did not serve its Creator," which is destined to stand in rebuke.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:39: And he says to him: "stand in judgment and acknowledge your deeds, and know whence you came and before whom you are destined to give judgment; and if you cannot answer, who can answer? And who can bear his sins, which are like fire to a garment, like a sword to the neck, like an arrow to the heart, like chains to the feet, like darkness to the eyes, like bitterness to the mouth, like a pit to the foot, like ploughing to the ears, like a stumbling block to strength, like evil days to old age, like sufferings to the body, like severance to the horn, like bitterness to death, like transgression to the Day of Judgment."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:40: There is one who dies in the midst of his days, and there is one who leaves the world in innocence. Happy is one whose fear is upon his face; happy is one who guards himself from his sin; happy is one who is humble; happy is one whose masses praise him; happy is one who is lowly in his own eyes; happy is one who inclines his ear to hear words of Torah; happy is one who hears words of Torah every day. The Torah of the Lord is perfect, standing before a person at the time he engages in his study, and says: "the Lord is with you, mighty man of valor; behold, I have come to teach you, therefore I went out to meet you, to greet you early and find you. Happy are you if you remember Me; happy are you if you hide Me in your heart; happy are you if you sustain Me; happy are you if you proclaim Me; and every day may your thoughts be of Me, for through Me your days shall be multiplied. Distance yourself from transgression and cleave to Torah and flee from authority, and be always in wisdom, and call upon your God always, for He will calm you and satisfy you and give you rest. And remember that you are a putrid drop, destined for dust and a pit; therefore distance yourself from rest and serve your God with joy, and it will be for your compassion, for the way is bent low and it will be for your reward and provision. If you do this, it will shine for you like the dawn, and God will command for you" - for if you serve your God with love and affection, happy are you in this world, and it will be good for you in the World to Come" - so far I have found.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:41: Further, similar words Rabbeinu Tam wrote in Sefer HaYashar (Gate 17), writing that a person should say to his heart: "my heart, my heart, do you not know that you were created only to return to dust? From the day of your existence, why have you not remembered your end? Do you not know that all the days you live upon the earth are like a fleeting shadow and like chaff driven from the threshing floor and like smoke from a chimney - your days are decreed and your life is cut short, and every day or night that passes over you, a portion of your life's portions is diminished, and every day you draw nearer to the grave and fly away without wings. Why have you not remembered that you are dust, and did you not know that you were formed from the earth? On whom did you rely that you rebelled? And why are you hasty and do not bring to mind that bitter day - the day when your counsel will be lost and your wisdom corrupted, the day your tongue cleaves to your palate, the day they will carry you on their shoulders and bear you and cast you upon the lowest earth, and reckon you for every deed, and crush you like dust, yet your fire will not be quenched; the day you will see the reckoning arrayed and the book opened and the scales of judgment and the cup of poison in the hand of the Lord - there you will drain its dregs and your soul will roar in its pains. And what will you answer for your willful sins? For then you will see the fruit of your deeds and find your reward."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:42: "And if you were to die the death of the beast and not be destined to give a reckoning, it would have been fitting for you to rejoice in your death; but you shall go to a place more bitter than death, to a place of gloom, a land of darkness and the shadow of death, where dread shall fall upon you and shame shall cover you and your garment shall be a heap of worms, and sulfur shall be scattered upon your body, leaving you no remnant. Is not that day terrible and dreadful, a day for which there is no ransom, a day of bitter weeping, of moaning and wailing, a day of dread and outcry, a day of desolation and groaning, a day of bitter lamentation, a day when you shall array mourning, watch upon watch, a day when God's wrath and jealousy shall burn and His fury shall pour out like fire, a day when griefs and pains shall multiply, a day when every man's hands shall be on his loins, a day when all his possessions shall be lost, a day when the soul shall depart and the body remain like a vessel full of shame, cast aside like a silent stone."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:43: "And now, son of man, to whom will you flee for help, or who will be your shelter? Will you not then say, woe is me, what have I done, why have I despised the word of the Lord and turned after the stubbornness of my heart, and with what shall I cover myself, for I am naked? Gather yourself and be ashamed and disgraced over your sin, and give thanks to your God while your soul is still in your body and before the stars of your twilight grow dark. Repent one day before your death; hold fast to discipline, do not let it go, for it is your life" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:44: We find that even Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was anxious and afraid of the judgments of the World to Come, as they said (Berachot 28b): when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill, his disciples entered to visit him; once he saw them, he began to weep. His disciples said to him, "our teacher, light of Israel, right-hand pillar, mighty hammer, why do you weep?" He said to them: "if they were leading me before a king of flesh and blood, who is here today and tomorrow in the grave - if he is angry with me, his anger is not eternal anger; if he imprisons me, his imprisonment is not eternal imprisonment; if he puts me to death, his death sentence is not an eternal death; and I could appease him with words and bribe him with money - even so I would weep. And now that they are leading me before the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, who lives and endures forever and ever - if He is angry with me, His anger is eternal anger; if He imprisons me, His imprisonment is eternal imprisonment; if He puts me to death, my death is an eternal death, and I cannot appease Him with words or bribe Him with money. And not only this, but there are before me two paths, one to the Garden of Eden and one to Gehinnom, and I do not know upon which of them they are leading me - shall I not weep?" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:45: The Rosh, of blessed memory, writes (Orchot Chayim, for Monday) - his words: "and your bed shall be soaked with tears, and your thoughts shall trouble you when you recall the anxiety of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai at the time of his passing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:46: They said (Masechet Sofrim, chapter 16, halacha 8) concerning the greatness of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, of blessed memory - they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not leave a single passage of Torah unstudied, and he studied Scripture and Targum, Midrash, Halachot and Aggadot, and parables - he studied everything. And so they said of him, that he said: "if all the heavens were parchment and all the trees quills and all the sea ink, it would not suffice to write the wisdom I learned from my teacher, and I did not take from the wisdom of the sages more than a fly that dips into the great sea and diminishes it by a mere trace" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:47: Our Sages, of blessed memory (Sukkah 28a), add further concerning the things he studied - they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not neglect Scripture, Mishnah, Halachot and Aggadot, the fine points of the Torah, the fine points of the Scribes, the leniencies and stringencies, the analogical inferences [gezerah shavah], the calculations of seasons, gematriot, the speech of ministering angels, the speech of demons, and the speech of palm trees, the parables of launderers, the parables of foxes, matters great and small - the great matter being the Account of the Chariot, the small matter being the discussions of Abaye and Rava - to fulfill what is said (Proverbs 8:21) "to cause those who love Me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:48: Further, I found chapters from the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, speaking of the matter of the beating of the grave; I have chosen to copy them here, to arouse the heart to fear:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:49: Tractate Chibbut HaKever [The Beating of the Grave]
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:51: How does a person die? Ministering angels come to him: one of the ministering angels and one of the angels of death, and one who records and one who is appointed with him, and he says to him, "arise, your end has come." He says to them, "my end has not yet come." Immediately he opens his eyes and sees an angel whose length is from one end of the world to the other, from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head full of eyes, his garment fire, his covering fire, all of him fire, and a knife in his hand, and a drop of gall hangs from it - from it he dies, from it he decays, from it his face turns pale. And he does not die until he sees the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, as it is said (Exodus 33:20) "for man shall not see Me and live" - in their life they do not see, but they see at their death, as it is said (Psalms 22:30) "before Him shall bow all who go down to the dust," etc. Immediately he testifies against himself concerning everything he did in this world, and he testifies and the Holy One, blessed be He, seals it; if he is righteous, he delivers his soul to its Master; if he is completely wicked, he stiffens his neck and strengthens his inclination. From this our Sages, of blessed memory, said, even at the death of a wicked person, his inclination overpowers him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:52: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: just as he stiffened his neck in this world, so it is stiffened for him at the time of his death, when he stands in judgment, as it is said (Psalms 112:10) "the wicked shall see it and be grieved," etc. And at the time of the righteous man's death, what does it say? (Isaiah 57:1) "the righteous perishes," etc. And at the time of the wicked man's death, what does it say? (II Samuel 23:6) "but the wicked shall be all of them as thorns," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:54: They asked Rabbi Elazar, what is the judgment of the grave like? He said to them: at the time a person departs from the world, the Angel of Death comes and sits upon his grave and strikes him with his hand and says to him, "arise, tell me your name." He says to him, "it is revealed and known before Him who spoke and the world came into being that I do not know my name." Immediately he inserts spirit and soul into his body and stands him up and holds him liable to judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:55: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: half fire and iron chains are in his hand. Once, his limbs are dislocated; a second time, his bones are dislocated, and ministering angels come and gather them and stand him up, and strike him a third time, and demand judgment from him, and judge him with every measure. On the first day and the second day they judge him thus; on the third day they judge him with blows - they strike him on his two eyes because he saw and did not tell [the truth]; and on his ears because he heard and did not tell; and on his lips because from his lips came words of frivolity; and on his tongue because it testified falsely; and on his feet because his feet hastened toward transgression. From this our Sages, of blessed memory, said, whoever hastens his feet toward transgression, the Angel of Death hastens toward him, and whoever slanders his fellow with an evil tongue, his death is by croup.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:57: Rabbi Meir said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: the day of judgment on which the Holy One, blessed be He, judges a person in the grave is harsher than the judgment of Gehinnom - the judgment of Gehinnom is for those from twenty years old and up, but the judgment of the grave applies even to the righteous, even to weaned infants, even to nursing babes. But our Sages, of blessed memory, said, one who dwells in the Land of Israel and dies on the eve of the Sabbath does not experience the judgment of the grave. And what should one do to be saved from the judgment of the grave? He should be a lover of acts of charity and a lover of rebukes and a lover of acts of kindness, and bring guests into his house, and pray his prayers with intent - even if he dies outside the Land, he will not experience it, as it is said (Jonah 2:3) "and he said, I called out of my distress to the Lord," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:58: Ben Azzai says: there are three judgments, each harsher than the other, and all three are before the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Akiva says: are all three before the Holy One, blessed be He? Is it not that the judgment of the grave is judged by itself, and the judgment of Gehinnom is judged by itself alone, and the judgment of Heaven is before the Holy One, blessed be He - if there is no judgment against him, they release him immediately, and if not, they judge him a lengthy judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:60: Rabbi Yosi said: come and see how much difference there is between a beast and a person. A beast, however much suffering it bears in the world - they slaughter it and skin it and there is no judgment upon it; but a person, how much suffering he bears in this world, and after his death, if he is completely righteous, they release him from judgment, and if he is completely wicked, they judge him with severe judgments.
